task_title: Add deterministic run data for fun evaluation

plan_review.notes: Alt A extend optional SimEvent log rejected because RunStats evidence must not depend on a debug sink. Alt B pure headless inference rejected because weapon/ability provenance is not reconstructable after transient queues clear. Alt C global event bus rejected as broader and riskier than this slice. Added boss-reward spell opportunities, canonical generated-item keys, one headless active clock, exact MAD policy, opportunity dedupe, shared normal/error finalizer, legacy/comparison tests, and smoke-vs-synthetic evidence boundaries.

rounds.notes: The review stage was restarted after the post-release sweep/viewer scope expansion. It rolled up two validated single-model findings across the final implementation: active-time timestamp ordering and malformed historical fun-report handling. Both were fixed with regression coverage.
Verified the complete runtime, evaluator, release workflow, persistence, and viewer diff after all fixes; full second pass found no remaining concerns.
Adjudication validated explicit baseline selector mismatch, stale same-SHA fun-report retention, and operational-error masking. All three were fixed with focused regression coverage.
Final complete-diff review after all fixes found no remaining concerns.

findings.detail: The new renderer tests assert on JavaScript source substrings inside the emitted HTML rather than on rendered DOM output. They verify code text is present but not that populated baseline-sweep selector and criterion rows render. Prefer state-driven rendered-markup assertions if the renderer gains an executable DOM harness.

independent_grade.notes: Final rebased release-sweep/index/viewer delta validated against HEAD 60f2be755. Diagnostic scoring remains non-blocking; sibling report publication removes stale same-SHA data, malformed reports degrade to null, and explicit baseline-sweep loading distinguishes not-found from operational failures. Runtime configured-level handling remains deterministic and regression-tested. All targeted unit, headless, viewer, typecheck, lint, and verify-fast checks passed. Test coverage is 4 because generated browser-script branches are currently source-asserted rather than executed under a DOM harness.
